chapterIntroductions.title: Words That Make the Choice Clear
chapterIntroductions.introduction: Mercury turns attention toward words, questions, and decisions. Read your card through the message waiting for a reply, the plan being discussed, or the story you repeat before choosing. Clear language helps when it names the actual question. It becomes more noise when explanation takes the place of an answer. Start with one conversation and listen for what has not been said plainly. The chapter dates describe where you are in the birthday year. The reading offers a way to examine what is already happening within that time, with the next choice left in your hands.
chapterIntroductions.closingReflection: Which word or question made a real choice clearer during this chapter?

chapterIntroductions.title: What You Want and What You Give
chapterIntroductions.introduction: Venus turns attention toward desire, value, and reciprocity. Your card can help you look at what you choose because you want it, what you accept because it is familiar, and what an exchange asks of both people. A small shared plan can reveal more than a broad statement about love. Notice whether you can name your own wish while hearing someone else's. Care works better when the terms are visible and a no can remain part of the conversation. Use the chapter to examine a real exchange without asking the reading to decide who belongs in your life.
chapterIntroductions.closingReflection: Where did you make an exchange more honest without losing your own wish?

chapterIntroductions.title: The Next Direct Action
chapterIntroductions.introduction: Mars turns attention toward action, boundaries, and the way you handle pressure. Read your card beside a task you are avoiding, a request you need to answer, or a disagreement waiting for a clearer point. A direct action has a purpose you can name. Force can become a substitute for that purpose when winning the moment matters more than doing the work. Choose a small next step with a finish condition. Let the other person's reaction supply information without making it the sole measure of whether your boundary is useful. Courage can be plain, steady, and specific.
chapterIntroductions.closingReflection: Which action served the task without turning the moment into a contest?

chapterIntroductions.title: More With a Clear Purpose
chapterIntroductions.introduction: Jupiter turns attention toward growth, generosity, and proportion. Your card can help you examine what is ready for more room and what would only become harder to hold at a larger size. Notice the promise made before the current work is complete, or the useful idea kept small because it has never been tested. Ask what a larger version would require in ordinary time, effort, and responsibility. The chapter does not promise luck or reward. It gives you a lens for deciding what deserves expansion and how to keep that expansion connected to a purpose you can actually support.
chapterIntroductions.closingReflection: What became more useful through growth, and what needed a smaller scope?

chapterIntroductions.title: A Limit You Can Keep
chapterIntroductions.introduction: Saturn turns attention toward structure, follow-through, and the limits that make a promise workable. Read your card beside a repeated task, an unclear obligation, or a standard that keeps moving. A useful limit protects a purpose. It becomes a punishment when the purpose disappears and more effort is always the answer. Name what is actually yours to carry and what counts as complete. One smaller agreement kept can give better information than a broad commitment followed by resentment. The chapter offers a place to examine responsibility plainly, with room to revise the arrangement rather than judge yourself for finding it difficult.
chapterIntroductions.closingReflection: What limit or agreement made responsibility more workable during this chapter?

chapterIntroductions.title: Changing the Part That Needs It
chapterIntroductions.introduction: Uranus turns attention toward freedom, fresh approaches, and experiments. Your card can help you distinguish a change that answers a real need from motion that simply interrupts an uncomfortable moment. Notice which rule no longer fits and which dependable part still serves the work. Try one revision small enough to examine. State what is changing and what you intend to keep, so others do not have to infer the whole answer from your movement. The chapter does not require a sudden event. It invites a clearer choice about what can be updated and how much continuity the useful change needs.
chapterIntroductions.closingReflection: Which change created useful room while keeping a dependable part intact?

chapterIntroductions.title: Room for Imagination and a Plain Fact
chapterIntroductions.introduction: Neptune turns attention toward imagination, uncertainty, and what can be released. Read your card beside an unfinished account, a hope you have not tested, or a task you keep carrying after its useful part is done. A softer approach can help you see more, while one plain fact keeps the choice grounded. Separate what you know from what you picture. If an ending is needed, name the work that belongs before it; if something remains open, let it be open without turning a story into proof. Use the actual dates shown, since this final chapter can be longer than the others.
chapterIntroductions.closingReflection: What could you put down while keeping one useful fact or practice?

notifications.title: Mercury Begins on {startLabel}
notifications.body: Your Mercury chapter starts on {startLabel}. Notice one conversation or decision that needs a clearer question. The reading is ready when you want to look ahead.

notifications.title: A Clearer Question Ahead
notifications.body: Mercury starts on {startLabel}. You can begin with the words you have been circling around. One plain question is enough to open the conversation.

notifications.title: Mercury Opens on {startLabel}
notifications.body: The next chapter starts on {startLabel}. Set aside one message, plan, or choice to examine through your Mercury reading when it opens.

notifications.title: Bring the Unsent Sentence
notifications.body: Your Mercury chapter opens on {startLabel}. Bring the thing you have not said plainly yet. There is room to read it before deciding what to do.

notifications.title: Your Mercury Chapter Is Open
notifications.body: Mercury runs from {startLabel} to {endLabel}. Read the card beside one actual conversation. Name the question before deciding which answer to use.

notifications.title: One Conversation at a Time
notifications.body: Your Mercury reading is open for {startLabel} to {endLabel}. Start with the message or choice nearest to you, and let one clear sentence be enough.

notifications.title: A Mercury Check-In
notifications.body: You are at the midpoint of the Mercury chapter. Which conversation became clearer, and which one still needs an actual answer rather than another explanation?

notifications.title: Return to the Real Question
notifications.body: Halfway through Mercury, you can revisit the question you began with. Notice what has been said plainly and what still belongs in the next conversation.

notifications.title: Venus Begins on {startLabel}
notifications.body: Your Venus chapter starts on {startLabel}. Choose one exchange to notice: what you want, what you give, and what has not been discussed yet.

notifications.title: Room for Your Own Wish
notifications.body: Venus starts on {startLabel}. Your own preference belongs in the picture too. Bring one shared plan you would like to understand more honestly.

notifications.title: Venus Opens on {startLabel}
notifications.body: The Venus chapter starts on {startLabel}. A relationship, value, or ordinary agreement can give you a concrete place to begin the reading.

notifications.title: Bring the Exchange That Matters
notifications.body: Your Venus reading opens on {startLabel}. Think of one exchange where you want more honesty. You can keep the question small and close to everyday life.

notifications.title: Your Venus Chapter Is Open
notifications.body: Venus runs from {startLabel} to {endLabel}. Read your card beside a real exchange and notice whether both people's wishes are visible in it.

notifications.title: Let Your Wish Be Present
notifications.body: Your Venus reading is open for {startLabel} to {endLabel}. Start with what you want and what you are offering. An honest difference can stay in view.

notifications.title: A Venus Check-In
notifications.body: At the midpoint of Venus, look at one exchange you have been noticing. Which term is clearer, and which preference still needs to be spoken?

notifications.title: Check What Feels Mutual
notifications.body: Halfway through Venus, return to one shared plan. You can ask what feels mutual now and leave room for your own answer to have changed.

notifications.title: Mars Begins on {startLabel}
notifications.body: Your Mars chapter starts on {startLabel}. Notice one task, boundary, or disagreement that needs a direct next step. The card offers a lens for that choice.

notifications.title: A Small Action Can Be Enough
notifications.body: Mars starts on {startLabel}. Bring a choice that has been waiting for movement. You do not need a grand gesture to begin looking at it.

notifications.title: Mars Opens on {startLabel}
notifications.body: The Mars chapter starts on {startLabel}. Name one action you want to examine and the purpose it should serve before opening the reading.

notifications.title: Bring the Next Step
notifications.body: Your Mars reading opens on {startLabel}. Think of one step that could be direct and useful. Let the question be about the work in front of you.

notifications.title: Your Mars Chapter Is Open
notifications.body: Mars runs from {startLabel} to {endLabel}. Read your card beside a concrete action or boundary. What would serve the task without turning it into a contest?

notifications.title: Choose a Useful Move
notifications.body: Your Mars reading is open for {startLabel} to {endLabel}. Begin with one action you can name and finish. A clear purpose gives the step somewhere to go.

notifications.title: A Mars Check-In
notifications.body: You are at the midpoint of Mars. Which action moved the actual work, and where has responding to pressure replaced choosing a useful next step?

notifications.title: Notice What Your Action Served
notifications.body: Halfway through Mars, look at one choice you acted on. Keep what served the purpose, and see whether the next step needs a clearer boundary.

notifications.title: Jupiter Begins on {startLabel}
notifications.body: Your Jupiter chapter starts on {startLabel}. Notice one area where more room could help and what a larger version would require from you in practice.

notifications.title: More Room for What Works
notifications.body: Jupiter starts on {startLabel}. Bring something useful that you would like to develop. You can consider growth at a size the real work can hold.

notifications.title: Jupiter Opens on {startLabel}
notifications.body: The Jupiter chapter starts on {startLabel}. Choose one plan to examine for scale, purpose, and the commitments that a larger version would create.

notifications.title: Bring the Plan You Can Support
notifications.body: Your Jupiter reading opens on {startLabel}. Think of what deserves more room and what is already asking enough of you. Both belong in the choice.

notifications.title: Your Jupiter Chapter Is Open
notifications.body: Jupiter runs from {startLabel} to {endLabel}. Read the card beside a real plan for growth. Name what is useful before deciding what should become larger.

notifications.title: Growth at a Useful Size
notifications.body: Your Jupiter reading is open for {startLabel} to {endLabel}. Start with what already works, then ask how much more room you can support with care.

notifications.title: A Jupiter Check-In
notifications.body: At the midpoint of Jupiter, examine one expansion or promise. Is its scope serving the purpose, and what does the actual work now tell you?

notifications.title: Keep the Useful Part of More
notifications.body: Halfway through Jupiter, notice what has grown clearer. A smaller scope can still serve a larger purpose when it leaves you able to keep the promise.

notifications.title: Saturn Begins on {startLabel}
notifications.body: Your Saturn chapter starts on {startLabel}. Bring one repeated task or obligation whose scope needs a clearer agreement. The reading can help you examine the terms.

notifications.title: A Workable Agreement Ahead
notifications.body: Saturn starts on {startLabel}. You can begin with one promise and the limit that would make it easier to keep. Responsibility can have a clear scope.

notifications.title: Saturn Opens on {startLabel}
notifications.body: The Saturn chapter starts on {startLabel}. Name a task that is yours to carry and what would count as complete before looking at the reading.

notifications.title: Bring the Promise You Want to Keep
notifications.body: Your Saturn reading opens on {startLabel}. Choose one commitment that matters. There is room to consider the smaller, clearer agreement that could support it.

notifications.title: Your Saturn Chapter Is Open
notifications.body: Saturn runs from {startLabel} to {endLabel}. Read your card beside a real responsibility. Examine its purpose, its limits, and the next piece that is actually yours.

notifications.title: A Clear Limit Can Help
notifications.body: Your Saturn reading is open for {startLabel} to {endLabel}. Start with one practical commitment. You can give it a finish point and room for an honest answer.

notifications.title: A Saturn Check-In
notifications.body: You are at the midpoint of Saturn. Which agreement is becoming workable, and which obligation still needs a limit or a clearer account of who carries it?

notifications.title: Notice What You Can Keep
notifications.body: Halfway through Saturn, look at a promise you have been carrying. What has become dependable, and what needs a more honest scope before you continue?

notifications.title: Uranus Begins on {startLabel}
notifications.body: Your Uranus chapter starts on {startLabel}. Notice a rule or method that no longer fits and a useful part you would want to keep during any change.

notifications.title: Room to Try Another Way
notifications.body: Uranus starts on {startLabel}. Bring one small change you are curious about. A modest trial can show more than imagining a completely different arrangement.

notifications.title: Uranus Opens on {startLabel}
notifications.body: The Uranus chapter starts on {startLabel}. Choose one possible revision and name the practical need it would answer before opening the reading.

notifications.title: Bring a Change You Can Examine
notifications.body: Your Uranus reading opens on {startLabel}. Think of one experiment small enough to try and understand. You can keep the dependable part beside the new idea.

notifications.title: Your Uranus Chapter Is Open
notifications.body: Uranus runs from {startLabel} to {endLabel}. Read the card beside a proposed change. What needs updating, and what should stay available while you test it?

notifications.title: Try the Part That Needs Changing
notifications.body: Your Uranus reading is open for {startLabel} to {endLabel}. Start with one useful revision. Say what you are keeping so the change has something to stand on.

notifications.title: A Uranus Check-In
notifications.body: At the midpoint of Uranus, review one change or trial. What did it show, and which dependable part helped you judge whether the revision was useful?

notifications.title: Keep What the Trial Taught You
notifications.body: Halfway through Uranus, you can return to the experiment with real information. Notice what opened useful room and what deserves a clearer or smaller change.

notifications.title: Neptune Begins on {startLabel}
notifications.body: Your Neptune chapter starts on {startLabel}. Bring one hope, unfinished account, or task you may be ready to put down. Keep one actual fact beside it.

notifications.title: A Little Room to Reconsider
notifications.body: Neptune starts on {startLabel}. You can bring an open question without forcing a complete answer. One plain fact can sit beside what you are still imagining.

notifications.title: Neptune Opens on {startLabel}
notifications.body: The Neptune chapter starts on {startLabel}. Name what you know and what remains a picture or possibility before using the reading to examine the difference.

notifications.title: Bring What Is Still Open
notifications.body: Your Neptune reading opens on {startLabel}. Think of one account that could become less forced. You can leave uncertainty visible while keeping a useful anchor.

notifications.title: Your Neptune Chapter Is Open
notifications.body: Neptune runs from {startLabel} to {endLabel}. Read your card beside an actual hope or unfinished task. Separate what you know from what you are picturing.

notifications.title: A Plain Fact Beside the Picture
notifications.body: Your Neptune reading is open for {startLabel} to {endLabel}. Begin with one open question. Let imagination have room while one useful fact keeps the choice close.

notifications.title: A Neptune Check-In
notifications.body: You are at the actual midpoint of Neptune. Which account has become clearer, and what can you release without leaving a necessary piece of work unfinished?

notifications.title: Let the Unneeded Part Rest
notifications.body: Halfway through Neptune, notice what you no longer need to keep explaining or carrying. Keep the useful lesson and see what present task has room to continue.

slides.title: Seven chapters to read with your life.
slides.body: Your birthdate gives the app a calculated set of cards and chapter dates. Each reading offers a way to notice a habit, a choice, or a useful next step.

slides.title: Start with what you recognize.
slides.body: Bring an actual conversation or task. Notice which parts fit, which parts do not, and what you want to choose next. The cards do not decide the answer for you.

slides.title: A focus, a change, and a resource.
slides.body: Long Range names the year's focus. Pluto names desired growth. Result offers a possible resource. Environment and Displacement appear when the calculated reading supplies those cards.

onboarding.profileIntroduction: Use a real calendar birthdate so the app can calculate your cards and chapter dates. Review the result before reading its meaning.
onboarding.dateExplanation: The calculation uses your calendar birthdate. Chapter dates belong to the birthday year shown in the app.
onboarding.questionLabel: What choice would you like to think about?
onboarding.questionHelp: A concrete conversation, plan, or task gives you a useful place to begin. You can keep this question to yourself.

errors.nameRequired: Enter the name you want shown.
errors.futureDate: Choose a birthdate that has already occurred.
errors.readingUnavailable: This reading is not available for that date. Check the entered date and try again.
errors.jokerUnsupported: December 31 sits outside the 52-card yearly library. This app does not calculate its period readings.

integrity.readingFrame: Here is a card pattern to put beside your question. Use what helps you see the choice more clearly.
integrity.footer: Card readings are offered for reflection and entertainment. They are not medical, financial, legal, or psychological advice.
integrity.meaningNote: Card meanings come from a symbolic tradition and the reviewed writing library. They do not establish facts about your character or predict events.
integrity.calculationNote: The app calculates card assignments and chapter dates before selecting the written reading. A calculated assignment is separate from the interpretation offered beside it.
integrity.dateNote: Use the start and end dates shown for the selected birthday year. The final Neptune chapter can be longer than the other chapters.
integrity.longRangeExplanation: A main theme to compare with the choices you are making across the birthday year.
integrity.plutoExplanation: A picture of growth you may want to work toward and the habits that make it difficult.
integrity.resultExplanation: A useful capacity to consider alongside Pluto. It is not a guaranteed reward or a forecast of how the year ends.
integrity.environmentExplanation: Read the useful side of the actual assigned card as support you may be able to use. Check what is available in your real circumstances.
integrity.displacementExplanation: The actual assigned card describes a place to examine responsibility and a growth edge. It does not make every difficulty a required lesson.
integrity.fixedCards: The fixed cards, Eight of Clubs, Jack of Hearts, and King of Spades, have no lifetime owe-and-owed pair. Use their own quiet, useful, and excessive forms instead. Their yearly Environment and Displacement fields remain absent when the engine supplies none.
integrity.semiFixedCards: Ace of Clubs and Two of Hearts are a semi-fixed pair, as are Seven of Diamonds and Nine of Hearts. For lifetime karma, the card you owe and the card you are owed are the same twin. These lifetime labels do not substitute for the actual yearly Environment or Displacement assignment.
integrity.absentEnvironment: The calculated reading supplies no Environment card for this year.
integrity.absentDisplacement: The calculated reading supplies no Displacement card for this year.
integrity.echoNote: An echo is shown only when the calculated reading explicitly marks an exact card relationship as an echo. A shared rank or suit does not establish one.
integrity.courtNote: Jack, Queen, and King describe roles anyone can hold. Read an actual person or your own posture; no age or gender is required and no arrival is promised.
integrity.significanceNote: Threshold, karmic, and structural name traditional rank emphasis. Karmic does not mean deserved punishment or a verified force.
integrity.fitNote: A passage that does not fit can be left aside. You do not need to reshape your experience to match a reading.
integrity.journalNote: Use a note to record what happened and what you chose, including where the reading did not fit.
integrity.versionNote: This library records its source and content version. Changes to writing should be logged as revisions rather than presented as something the earlier reading always said.

shareCopy.captionTemplate: I'm reading {cardName} through {planet}. The question I'm considering: {reflection}
shareCopy.yearlyCaptionTemplate: {cardName} as {roleLabel}: {readingTitle}. A yearly theme to think with.
shareCopy.privacyNote: Review what you share. Leave your birthdate, private question, and personal notes out unless you choose to include them.
shareCopy.unavailableMessage: Sharing is unavailable here. You can copy the caption instead.
shareCopy.dateUnavailableSubtitle: A chapter in my birthday year
shareCopy.readingUnavailableMessage: Open an available reading before making a share caption.

connectors.template: Place this chapter beside {longRangeCardName}, the year's main focus. Where does the same question about your attention appear in an ordinary choice?
Use {longRangeCardName} to widen the view, then return to one small scene in this chapter. The yearly focus is most useful when you can see what it asks of that actual choice.
The period card and {longRangeCardName} offer different scales of attention. Compare them without requiring the same answer from both.
Read this chapter beside {plutoCardName}, your Pluto card. What desired change would make the next step more honest?
With {plutoCardName} as Pluto, notice the habit that makes a wanted change harder. Keep the habit concrete enough to recognize in the present conversation or task.
Read {plutoCardName} and {resultCardName} together: a change you want to work toward, and a possible capacity you can practice alongside that work.
Your Result card, {resultCardName}, offers a possible resource to consider. Which part of its useful form could you practice in this chapter?
Keep {resultCardName} beside the current choice as a picture of useful capacity. The reading does not establish how the year ends.
Look for one small use of {resultCardName} in the work already available. A practiced skill is easier to recognize than an outcome you are waiting for.
Your assigned Environment card is {environmentCardName}. Name a real source of support that fits its useful side, then decide how you could use it for this task.
Bring {environmentCardName}, the year's support card, to a clear request. Ask for the help that is actually available rather than assuming the whole need is covered.
Support pictured by {environmentCardName} works through a real person, capacity, or arrangement. Keep its actual limits visible as you use it in this chapter.
Your assigned Displacement card, {displacementCardName}, describes the seat you occupy this year. Which responsibility or growth edge becomes visible from that place?
Read {displacementCardName} beside the task in front of you. Name the part that is yours to practice without turning every difficulty into an assignment.
Keep {environmentCardName} and {displacementCardName} in view together: support you can use, and a seat that asks something specific of you.
The calculated reading marks {echoCardName} as an echo of {echoRoleLabel}. Compare the two meanings as a familiar theme, then check how it appears in a present choice.

The calculated period card is also {matchingYearRole}, {matchingCardName}. Read the same card through both positions; the repeated identity is a reason to compare the meanings, not a promise of a stronger event.
You can compare these readings without making them tell one complete story. Keep the part that helps you see the actual choice, and leave the rest available to reconsider.

runtimeNotes.yearlyLookup: Use the bible slug plus the role slug. Role slugs are long-range, pluto, result, environment, and displacement. The 260 records cover meanings available for lookup; they do not assign any card to a user.
runtimeNotes.yearlyEligibility: Render Environment or Displacement copy only when the selected calculated packet has a real non-null card for that role. A library record or another lifetime card is not evidence of a yearly assignment.
runtimeNotes.fixedAndSemiFixed: Check the actual engine packet for yearly eligibility. Fixed cards are 8♣, J♥, and K♠. Semi-fixed lifetime twins are A♣/2♥ and 7♦/9♥. Do not apply the August report's seven-card blanket exclusion to yearly records.
runtimeNotes.birthdayYear: Use the selected birthday-year packet for all card and date substitutions. Do not borrow cards or dates from another year or the illustrative August sample.

notificationMoments.before14: Schedule relative to the actual chapter start, fourteen calendar days before it.
notificationMoments.before1: Schedule one calendar day before the actual start.
notificationMoments.midpoint: Compute from the actual start and end using the existing calendar conventions. Neptune may be longer than 52 days; do not hard-code day 26 for it.

notificationVariables.startLabel: Formatted actual start date of this notification's chapter.
notificationVariables.endLabel: Formatted actual end date of the same chapter.

runtimeNotes.notificationDispatch: These records are copy only. Their presence does not schedule, send, subscribe, or enable notifications. Use the app's actual delivery state and preferences.
runtimeNotes.missingNotificationDates: Do not show a date-bearing notification if its dates are absent, invalid, or from the wrong birthday year. Never expose unresolved placeholders.
runtimeNotes.connectorSelection: Select at most one or two connectors for a reading. Use the one that clarifies the actual choice. Do not concatenate the library into a second reading.
runtimeNotes.connectorVariables: Substitute only displayed assigned card names and verified relation labels. Render a connector only when every item in requires is available and its relation is true. verifiedEcho and verifiedExactMatch are eligibility flags, not visible text.
runtimeNotes.echoEligibility: Use verified-echo only when the packet explicitly marks ECHO and identifies the exact role. Use verified-identical-card only after an exact card-code match. A shared suit, rank, or loose theme never creates an echo or an activation window.
runtimeNotes.shareVariables: Use current displayed cardName, planet, readingTitle, reflection, roleLabel, startLabel, and endLabel as appropriate to the chosen template. Omit the date subtitle or use dateUnavailableSubtitle if real dates are unavailable. Do not substitute private user text into a public caption without the user choosing it.
runtimeNotes.literalCopy: All readings and connective sentences are authored static text. Runtime selects and substitutes verified display values; it does not generate paragraphs by combining rank, suit, and role kernels.
runtimeNotes.courtRoles: Do not replace court role wording with a forecast about a man, woman, younger person, admirer, or authority arriving.
runtimeNotes.scope: This writing makes no claims about launches, pricing, paywalls, subscriptions, delivery setup, deployment, or changes to the engine.
